title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array (In Place)
hints: In a sorted array, duplicates are adjacent.
Keep a write index; copy an element forward only when it differs from the last written one.
jsBridge: A read/write two-pointer pass over an `inout` array, then `removeLast(k)` to truncate. JS mutates arrays in place freely, while Swift requires `inout` and `&` to make that visible.

compass.q: JS `arr.length = k` truncates in place. What's the Swift equivalent, and is it O(1)?
In-place two pointers vs `Array(Set(nums)).sorted()`: which preserves stability and memory?
What does `removeSubrange(k...)` do to capacity? Does the buffer shrink?
Does in-place mutation ever matter in app code, or only in interviews?
